summary: NNPC Ltd and TotalEnergies run two schemes for Nigerians: the National Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMSS), a yearly grant for 100- and 200-level undergraduates at Nigerian universities, and the TotalEnergies International Scholarship (TIS), a fully funded Master's in France in management science, engineering or geosciences. Winners have strong grades, apply early with complete documents, and do well in a computer-based aptitude test and later selection stages.
lookfor: Master's (TIS): at least a 2:1, degree within the last 5 years, NYSC completed, in a field relevant to oil and gas
Master's (TIS): a sensible French Master's programme choice through Campus France
Undergraduate (NMSS): UTME of 200+, and CGPA of at least 2.5/5.0 for 200-level applicants
Performance in the computer-based aptitude test (quantitative, verbal, logical reasoning and current affairs, as reported)
Complete, consistent documents and reachable contact details
cycle: Master's (TIS): the 2026/27 round closed 31 Jan 2026 (2025/26 also closed 31 Jan), so expect the 2027/28 round to open late 2026 and close around end of January 2027 - check the current guidance. Undergraduate (NMSS): usually mid-year; the 2025 round closed 1 July 2025.

eligibility.no: Both schemes are for Nigerians only.

eligibility.q: Master's: do you hold at least a 2:1 obtained within the last five years?
eligibility.no: Consider PTDF Overseas (accepts 2:2 with industry experience) or Chevening.
Apply in the round after your passing-out.

eligibility.q: Master's: is your intended programme in management science, engineering or geosciences related to oil and gas?
eligibility.no: TIS will not fund other fields; look at Chevening, Commonwealth or DAAD.

eligibility.q: Master's: do you have less than about three years of work experience?
eligibility.no: This was reported by Legit.ng for 2026/27 - check the current guidance. Experienced professionals may suit Chevening better.

eligibility.q: Undergraduate: are you a full-time 100- or 200-level student at an NUC-accredited university with UTME 200+ (and CGPA 2.5+ if 200 level)?
Are you free of other oil and gas industry scholarships?
eligibility.no: NMSS excludes holders of similar oil and gas scholarships. Choose one.

steps.title: Choose your track: NMSS or International Master's
steps.why: The two schemes have different rules, windows and forms. Mixing them up wastes time.
do: Open the official TotalEnergies scholarship portal and read both scheme descriptions.
Undergraduate at 100 or 200 level: follow the NMSS steps.
Graduate with a 2:1 and NYSC done: follow the Master's (TIS) steps.
Note the support email shown on the portal for questions.
tips: The portal FAQ says the process is free and test formats change every year.
avoid: Paying anyone who claims to 'facilitate' the scholarship.
check: I know which track I am on.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility and understand selection
steps.why: The first screen is strict on grade, date and NYSC rules.
do: Master's: read the last official advert (2025/26) and check 2:1, degree date within 5 years, NYSC, and field.
Undergraduate: check UTME 200+, CGPA 2.5+ (200 level), and NUC accreditation of your university.
Note the stages: online application, shortlisting, computer-based aptitude test, then further selection.
Write two backup awards (e.g. PTDF, Chevening for Master's; NLNG, Agbami for undergraduates).
tips: Only shortlisted candidates are contacted - silence usually means not shortlisted.
avoid: Applying with a degree older than five years.
check: I meet every rule for my track.

steps.title: Master's: pick your French Master's programme
steps.why: TIS funds study at French universities. A programme that fits your degree and the energy sector strengthens your case.
do: Open Campus France Nigeria and use 'Find your programme'.
Filter by Master's, English-taught (unless you speak French), and your field (engineering, geosciences, management).
Shortlist 2-3 programmes and note their entry rules and start dates.
Write one sentence on how each links to oil and gas or the energy transition.
tips: Public universities were preferred in the 2026/27 advert as reported.
avoid: Choosing a programme with no link to the energy sector.
check: I have 2-3 French programmes with a clear energy link.

steps.title: Build your timeline and watch for the opening
steps.why: Windows are short and announced on the official site. Early submitters avoid portal jams.
do: Master's: set reminders from November to check the portal weekly; aim to submit by mid-January.
Undergraduate: set reminders from April to check for NMSS; aim to submit in the first week.
Create a folder for scans named 'TotalEnergies'.
Use an email and phone number you will keep for a year - the portal FAQ asks for reachable contacts.
tips: The site may open in French by default; switch to English.
avoid: Using adverts on blogs as your only source.
check: My reminders and folder are ready.

steps.title: Master's: gather degree, NYSC and ID documents
steps.why: Missing or inconsistent documents fail the first screen.
do: Request your degree certificate (or statement of result) and transcript from your university's Academic Office.
Find your NYSC discharge certificate.
Apply for or renew your international passport through the Nigeria Immigration Service portal - you will need it for France.
Check names match across all documents; swear an affidavit if not.
Scan everything clearly.
tips: Transcripts can take 4-8 weeks in many Nigerian universities - ask now.
avoid: Waiting for the advert before requesting transcripts.
check: Degree, transcript, NYSC and passport scans are ready.

steps.title: Undergraduate: gather UTME, admission and CGPA proof
steps.why: NMSS checks your UTME score, admission and (200 level) CGPA.
do: Print your UTME result slip and JAMB admission letter.
200 level: get your 100-level result or transcript from your department.
Take a passport photograph and scan your student ID card.
Scan everything clearly.
tips: Ask your department for a stamped result if the official transcript is slow.
avoid: Rounding up your CGPA - it will be checked.
check: UTME, admission letter, result and photo are scanned.

steps.title: Master's: write a two-page CV
steps.why: The official advert asks you to attach a CV; it is often the first thing screeners read.
do: Top: name, contacts, degree, class, year.
Education: degree with class; final-year project title.
Experience: NYSC, internships (SIWES), jobs - with one result each.
Skills: software, lab or field skills, languages (note any French).
Keep to two pages, clean layout, PDF.
tips: Put energy-relevant projects and SIWES placements near the top.
avoid: Photos, date of birth paragraphs and long hobby lists.
check: My CV fits two pages and shows my energy-sector link.

steps.title: Master's: prepare your motivation statement
steps.why: If the form or later stages ask why you want the programme, a ready, focused answer makes you stand out.
do: Paragraph 1: the energy-sector problem you care about in Nigeria.
Paragraph 2: what you have done so far (degree, project, NYSC, internship).
Paragraph 3: why this French programme - name modules or labs.
Paragraph 4: your career plan in Nigeria's energy sector after the Master's.
Keep a 300-word and a 500-word version ready.
tips: Mention willingness to learn French - it shows you are serious about France.
check: My statement names the programme and my career goal.
steps.prompt: Why you want this Master's in France and how it fits your career in Nigeria's energy sector.
steps.limit: Not confirmed - check the current form

steps.title: Line up referees for the French universities
steps.why: TotalEnergies did not publish a reference rule, but French Master's admissions usually ask for recommendation letters.
do: Choose a lecturer or project supervisor and an NYSC or work supervisor.
Email them your CV, transcript and motivation statement.
Ask if they will write a letter and give them a deadline two weeks ahead.
Save their official emails and phone numbers.
tips: Official university email addresses carry more weight.

steps.title: Create your account and fill the form
steps.why: Applications are accepted only through the official website.
do: Go to the TotalEnergies Nigeria scholarship portal and create an account.
Choose NMSS or TIS ('Get Started') and fill each section.
Master's: note the Candidate Reference Number - the 2025/26 advert said it is needed to complete the application.
Upload your CV and supporting documents.
tips: Fill the form on a laptop with stable internet.
check: Every section is complete and I have my reference number.

steps.title: Proofread, submit early and keep proof
steps.why: Errors or late submission end your chance; only shortlisted candidates are contacted.
do: Check every name, date and grade against your documents.
Submit at least a week before the deadline.
Screenshot the confirmation and save the email.
tips: Write down your login and reference number.
check: I have saved proof of submission.

steps.title: Prepare for the aptitude test
steps.why: Shortlisted candidates sit a computer-based test; it is the main filter.
do: Practise quantitative reasoning (percentages, ratios, data tables) daily.
Practise verbal and logical reasoning with timed sets.
Read Nigerian and energy news for current affairs questions.
Read the invitation carefully for the centre or online instructions.
tips: The portal FAQ says there are no official past questions and the format changes yearly - practise skills, not memorised answers.
check: I have done at least five timed practice sets.

links.t: Watch: 2026/2027 NNPCL/TOTALENERGIES SCHOLARSHIP INTERVIEW INSIGHTS (Abasiofon Moses)

steps.title: Master's: prepare for interview and French admission
steps.why: Later stages can include interviews and securing admission to the French programme before the award is final.
do: Practise answers: Why France? Why this programme? How will it help Nigeria's energy sector?
Follow any instructions to apply to the chosen French programmes.
Start learning basic French (an online course or the Alliance Francaise).
Prepare for the French student visa process via Campus France Nigeria.
tips: Keep your passport valid for the whole study period.
avoid: Resigning from a job before you have a written award.
check: I have a written award or a clear next step from TotalEnergies.

steps.title: Undergraduate: accept the award and keep your grades
steps.why: NMSS pays yearly until you finish, as long as you stay in good standing.
do: Follow the award email exactly to submit any extra documents and bank details through the official process.
Keep copies of every award letter.
Keep your CGPA up; send results when asked.
avoid: Sharing bank details with anyone outside the official process.
check: I have accepted the award in writing.

faq.a: No. The official portal says the process is free. Never pay anyone.

faq.q: Do I need to speak French?
faq.a: Not necessarily - many French Master's are taught in English, but learning basic French helps you live there and in interviews.
Recent reports say up to N200,000 a year until graduation. Check the current advert.

faq.q: I graduated six years ago. Can I apply for the Master's?
faq.a: No - the degree must be from the last five years. Consider Chevening or PTDF.

faq.q: I did not hear back. What does that mean?
faq.a: Only shortlisted candidates are contacted, so you were probably not shortlisted. Prepare for the next round.
